**Research resumed on 2026-10-09 toward [10 substantial findings](frontier/TEN-FINDINGS.md): 8 accepted, 2 remaining.** The fourth, [R010 — factor-count residues and PD independence](frontier/findings/R010-complex-modes-PD-independence.md), has passed independent proof and significance reviews plus parent verification. **[R012 — uniform Gaussian propeller stability](frontier/findings/R012-uniform-gaussian-propeller-stability.md) is accepted as the sixth substantial finding.** Its deficit controls squared distance to a three-sector propeller with one constant for every dimension and finite cell count, without cell-mass constraints. The original proof passes independent review without repairs; the final significance review judges the control of disappearing labels substantial. Parent reproduction passes. The distance exponent is sharp, the constant is implicit, and worldwide priority remains uncertified. I39 records an unresolved Haldane-disorder gap. I41 independently passes I40’s technical Gaussian waiting-time deduction without repairs; I42 likewise passes I41’s technical four-time comparison and supporting partial results without repairs. The Rademacher fair-start density bound remains open. I45 independently passes I44’s attributed symmetric equality argument and its three supporting results without repairs. Symmetric equality is technically closed under the pinned premises, with full Liu–Sun–Xiong attribution. I47 independently passes I46’s facet-independent planar exponent-10 stability proof without repairs. I48 classifies it as technical, giving an explicit reduction through classical planar geometry and weighted dual Cheeger estimates. [R013 — higher-dimensional logarithmic stability](frontier/findings/R013-higher-dimensional-logarithmic-stability.md) is now accepted as the seventh substantial finding: I50 passes I49’s original proof without repairs, I51 judges the contribution substantial, and parent reproduction passes. For arbitrary ball-bounded symmetric convex bodies in every fixed dimension n≥3, the logarithmic deficit controls a finite power of distance to common complementary-block dilation pairs, with exponent depending only on dimension. I52 records finite-time and conditional standard-map entropy deductions. I54 now proposes the constant additive-loss theorem through a quantitative initial scale and the pinned limiting contradiction, plus a restricted tangent-direction estimate. I57 passes the original additive-entropy proof and restricted projective estimates without repairs; parent reproduction passes. I58 classifies the bound and restricted estimates as technical consequences of the accepted source operations; parent reproduction passes, so this route does not increase the substantial count. I55 passes I53’s original fixed-dimensional Wasserstein stability proof without repairs. I56 classifies it as technical, with a full reduction through classical tensor regularity; both parent replays pass. I59 records averaged normalization and compatibility estimates, a dependent radial-family bound, and explicit obstructions; the dimension-uniform entropy target remains unproved and unrefuted. Parent evidence reproduction passes. I61 proposes a dimension-independent coefficient-extraction estimate using paired spectral equations, plus a repair preserving bounded coefficient energy. I63 passes the original theorem, repair and scoped supporting results without repairs. I64 judges the uniform coefficient bridge substantial; both parent reproductions pass. [R014 — dimension-uniform coefficient extraction](frontier/findings/R014-uniform-coefficient-extraction.md) is accepted as the eighth substantial finding. Global algebra rounding and the unrestricted entropy theorem remain open. I60 closes its slice transfer as technical, refutes three stronger proposals and leaves the same-density two-union integral-cover target open. Parent evidence reproduction passes. I62 completes bounded-rank covers and explicit obstructions to two attempted general constructions; its same-density two-union target remains unproved and unrefuted. Parent evidence checks pass, with no substantial nomination. The delayed I29 common-base entropy report also completes a sharp technical corollary, with parent reproduction passing and no count increment. Two further substantial findings remain.
